documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M here to set up care. Was with his old PCP about ten years; wants somewhere he can actually get someone on the phone. Retired from driving long-haul last year, living in Easthampton on his own.

Hx per pt: blood pressure and cholesterol for a long time, diabetes for years, always pills only. Blocked arteries in the right leg; a vascular surgeon did a bypass on that leg in 2019 and he walks fine. Gallbladder out laparoscopically 2012, left groin hernia mesh repair 2008.

Meds (brought bottles): amlodipine 10 daily, metformin 1000 BID with meals, atorvastatin 40 at bedtime, aspirin 81. Takes them, occasionally forgets the evening metformin on the road days when he was working, better now.
Allergies: none to meds.

FH: father had an MI at 54 and dropped dead at 61 (cardiac arrest). Mother had a stroke at 74, also on BP pills. Older brother diabetic and hypertensive.
SH: smokes a pack a day, started at 24, so about 40 pk-yr. Has tried cold turkey twice, lasted a week. Not interested in quitting today but will listen. Beer on weekends, 2-3. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, no exertional breathlessness. No leg pain walking now. No foot sores. Vision fine, last eye exam about 2 yrs ago.

Exam: BP and pulse in flowsheet. Overweight, comfortable. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd soft, healed lap port scars, no hernia. Right leg: healed medial thigh and below-knee bypass incisions. Feet warm, no ulcers or calluses, monofilament intact both feet, DP/PT diminished bilaterally. No edema.

A/P
1. Type 2 DM - A1c, CMP, UACR today. Continue metformin. Eye exam letter needed - gave him the optometry list.
2. HTN - acceptable today on amlodipine 10.
3. Hyperlipidemia / PAD s/p R fem-pop - lipids today, atorvastatin 40 and aspirin continue. Walk daily.
4. Tobacco - brief advice to quit, he declines meds for now. Qualifies for lung screening; LDCT ordered, he agreed.
5. HCM - HCV and HIV once today, both ok with him. Request old records for colonoscopy, vaccines. Flu/COVID/pneumococcal at a nurse visit next month.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Walter, your labs from Tuesday are back. A1c is 7.6, a little over our target of 7 but not far. Kidney numbers and liver tests are fine, blood counts normal, and the urine protein test is normal. LDL cholesterol is 96. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. No changes for now; we'll go over it in December. Keep chipping away at the cigarettes.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
38 pages received from prior primary care office. Indexed:
- Problem list: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, PAD, tobacco use.
- Vascular surgery operative summary, 2019: right femoral-popliteal bypass for peripheral arterial disease, uncomplicated.
- Screening colonoscopy 2018: normal to cecum, no polyps; repeat at 10 years.
- Immunizations: Tdap 05/2017. Pneumococcal not documented.
- Lab flowsheets 2020-2023, A1c mostly in the 7s.
Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old records. Bypass and colonoscopy history confirmed; colonoscopy next due 2028. Tdap entered. No pneumococcal on file - PCV20 at the October nurse visit.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu, pneumonia and COVID shots per PCP. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. High-dose flu L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid, updated COVID L deltoid lower site. Tolerated, waited 15 min, no issues. VIS given. Reminded him the lung scan is booked for 11/8.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: current smoker, approximately 40 pack-years, age 64.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Upper abdomen unremarkable on limited images. Status post cholecystectomy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Three-month check. Feeling fine. Lung CT came back clean, relieved. Still a pack a day; says winter is the worst time to try. Taking his pills. Walks to the post office and back most days, no leg pain.
O: Vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Feet warm, no lesions, pulses diminished both feet as before.
A/P: DM2 - A1c and BMP today. HTN fine on amlodipine. PAD stable on aspirin/statin. Tobacco - offered patch or varenicline, he'd rather not. Next visit March.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry report, exam date 02/14/2024.
Patient: Walter Weiss. Reason: annual diabetic eye exam.
VA corrected 20/25 OD, 20/20 OS. IOP normal both eyes. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: repeat dilated exam in one year. Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine DM/HTN visit. Admits a lot of takeout over the winter. No hypoglycemia symptoms, no polyuria. Eye letter in: no retinopathy.
Exam: as charted for vitals. Cor RRR, lungs clear. Foot check: skin intact, monofilament normal, pedal pulses faint both sides, unchanged.
A1c drawn. Diet talk - he's going to cut the soda. Still smoking, not ready. Same meds. See in July with fasting labs.

documents.title: Refill request

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sorry about last month, he says. Doing ok. Gave up regular soda in the spring. Walking more now the weather's nice. Cigarettes about the same, a pack most days.
Exam: vitals as above. Heart and lungs unremarkable. Feet: warm, intact skin, sensation normal, pulses diminished bilat, healed R leg incisions. No edema.
Plan: fasting A1c, lipids, BMP, urine microalbumin today. Meds unchanged. Medicare wellness visit in September, flu shot then or after.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.
Health risk assessment reviewed: lives alone in a second-floor apartment, drives, does own shopping and cooking (mostly simple). No falls this year. Hearing ok. Sleep fine. PHQ-2 0. Cognitive screen normal (3-word recall 3/3, clock normal).
Tobacco: 1 ppd, precontemplative; advised again.
Alcohol: weekend beer only.
Advance directive: none; given forms, would name a close friend - he'll think on it.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2018 normal, due 2028. LDCT 11/2023 negative - repeat ordered for November. AAA screen due as a male smoker 65-75 - ultrasound ordered. RSV vaccine today. Flu/COVID/Shingrix next month at nurse visit.
Exam: vitals charted. Well appearing. Heart regular, lungs clear, no carotid bruit. Feet unchanged.
Written prevention plan given.
Labs: CMP and CBC today.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMINAL AORTA, AAA SCREENING
Indication: male, 65, current smoker.
Findings: The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum anteroposterior diameter 2.1 cm, measured outer wall to outer wall in the infrarenal segment. No focal dilatation. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.
reports.conclusion: No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Normal aortic caliber, 2.1 cm.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high-dose), COVID 2024-25 and Shingrix #1 today. Did fine with RSV last month. Shingrix #1 R deltoid, flu L deltoid, COVID L deltoid 1 inch below. Warned the shingles shot can knock him out for a day. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months - flagged for January visit.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (annual)
Comparison: 11/08/2023.
Findings: Lungs clear without nodule. No consolidation. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size. No adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Scan results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Walter - both scans are good news. The aorta ultrasound was normal, no aneurysm, and that one doesn't need repeating. The lung CT again shows no nodules. Next lung scan November 2025. You know what I'll say about the smoking. See you in January for the second shingles shot.

documents.title: RE: Scan results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks Doc. Good to hear. I know, I know.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check-in. Holidays were quiet. Took the first shingles shot hard, sore and wiped out about a day, game for #2 anyway. Smoking unchanged. No chest discomfort, breathing ok on stairs, legs fine walking.
Exam: BP/HR flowsheet. Cor regular, lungs clear. Feet warm, no breaks in skin, pulses diminished both, monofilament intact.
Plan: A1c + BMP. Shingrix #2 today, series done. Continue amlodipine, metformin, atorvastatin 40, ASA. Eye exam due in Feb - reminded. RTC spring.

No known drug allergies.

documents.title: Right eye going dark
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. Something odd the last week or so. A few times my right eye goes black from the top down like a shade, stays that way a couple minutes, then it's back like nothing happened. Feel fine otherwise. Is this something or nothing?

orders.reason: transient monocular vision loss, right eye

documents.title: Call re: transient vision loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called him after his message. Episodes of right-eye blackout lasting minutes, several over about a week, full recovery each time. None now. Denies double vision, weakness, numbness, trouble speaking or facial droop.
Discussed that this can be a warning sign of a stroke. Offered ED evaluation today; he prefers not unless it happens again. The vascular clinic at the outside cardiology group that does our PAD patients can see him Monday 5/5 - urgent referral sent and call placed to their scheduler. Told him to take his aspirin every day and to call 911 for any episode with weakness, speech change or one that doesn't clear. He repeated that back.

conditions.label: Transient ischemic attack
conditions.note: amaurosis fugax, right eye; per outside cardiology, letter pending

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw cardiology vascular clinic 5/5. We do not have their note yet. Per Walter: they told him the eye spells were a mini-stroke affecting the eye, his eye exam there was normal, and to keep taking the baby aspirin every day, no new pills. He hasn't had more since. Also mentions they said his cholesterol and sugar were up on their bloodwork.
No weakness, numbness or speech trouble.
Exam: BP/HR flowsheet. Alert, speech fluent, face symmetric, strength full and equal, gait normal. Cor RRR. Lungs clear.
A/P
1. TIA, amaurosis fugax R eye - per cardiology, continue aspirin 81. Added to problem list. Will review their plan when the letter comes. Records request sent.
2. Tobacco - this is the conversation to have. Strong advice to quit; offered varenicline or patches again. He says he'll cut down on his own.
3. DM2/HTN/HLD - their labs pending to us.
RTC Sept for wellness visit.

documents.title: Outside cardiology consultation (vascular clinic)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - VASCULAR CLINIC CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/05/2025
Referring: primary care
Reason: transient monocular visual loss, right eye

HPI: 66-year-old man with PAD (prior right fem-pop bypass), hypertension, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Over about two weeks he has had several spells in which vision in the right eye is lost as if a curtain is lowered, each lasting a few minutes, with complete recovery. He also notes occasional lightheadedness and mild headaches. No double vision, fainting, or arm or leg weakness.
Meds: amlodipine, metformin; atorvastatin 40 mg nightly; aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father MI age 54, sudden cardiac death age 61; mother ischemic stroke age 74, hypertension; older brother diabetes and hypertension.
Social: smokes 1 pack daily; social alcohol.

Exam: BP 158/92, pulse 76. Fundi normal between episodes. Neurologic examination nonfocal.
Labs (drawn today): LDL 112 mg/dL, above goal. HbA1c 8.2%, above target.

Impression: Transient ischemic attack manifesting as amaurosis fugax, right eye.
Plan: antiplatelet therapy - continue aspirin 81 mg daily; no additional agent. Smoking cessation strongly advised. Risk factors to be addressed with primary care. Return as needed.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology letter from 5/5 reviewed, finally in. TIA (amaurosis fugax R) confirmed, aspirin alone. LDL 112, A1c 8.2 on their draw. BP 158/92 there; ours 6/10 was fine. Will go over at September visit.

Subsequent AWV.

Tobacco: still about a pack a day. We talked about the eye spell being a warning; he says he knows. Declines medication again.
Advance directive: still hasn't filled out the forms.
Prevention: flu high-dose and 2025-26 COVID today. Lung CT due - ordered. Colonoscopy due 2028. Vaccines otherwise up to date (PCV20, Tdap 2017, Shingrix x2, RSV).
Exam: vitals charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Neuro grossly nonfocal. Feet warm, intact, pulses diminished as before.
Labs: CMP, lipids, urine microalbumin. A1c at next visit.
Personalized prevention plan printed.

documents.title: Pt call - recent hospitalization
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called to let us know he was admitted 10/8 through Saturday 10/11 at an outside hospital for a heart attack. Says they did a heart cath and put in a stent. Came home with new pills, reading off bottles: clopidogrel 75 daily, metoprolol succinate 25 daily, atorvastatin 80 (told to stop the 40s), nitroglycerin under the tongue as needed. Still on amlodipine, metformin, aspirin. Has not needed the nitro. No chest pain today. Feels tired.
We have no records - request sent to hospital. Post-hospital visit booked with PCP 10/21. Advised to bring all bottles. Reviewed 911 for chest pain not relieved by 1 nitro in 5 min.

documents.title: PCP review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Agree with plan. Will reconcile meds at the visit next week.

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet under the tongue every 5 minutes as needed for chest pain, up to 3

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. RN contact 10/13 (within 2 business days of discharge).
Hospital records not yet received. History from patient: on 10/8 he had several hours of a pressing, tight feeling in the middle of his chest that went into his left shoulder at times; drove himself to the ED (we discussed that). Told he had a heart attack without the full ST elevation type, kept in the cardiac unit on a heparin drip, then cath the next day with one stent. Home Saturday.
Since: tired, no chest pain, hasn't used nitro, no breathlessness, no bleeding or black stools. Cardiac rehab is calling him to set up. Cardiology follow-up 11/12.
Meds reconciled from bottles:
- aspirin 81 daily
- clopidogrel 75 daily
- atorvastatin 80 nightly (40 stopped)
- metoprolol succinate 25 daily
- amlodipine 10 daily
- metformin 1000 BID
- nitroglycerin 0.4 SL prn
Exam: BP/HR flowsheet, pulse slower on the beta blocker. Comfortable. Right radial site healed. Cor RRR, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. NSTEMI s/p stent - DAPT, high-intensity statin, BB per cardiology. Don't stop clopidogrel without talking to cardiology. Nitro use reviewed. Rehab - encouraged to go.
2. Tobacco - discussed plainly that this is the single biggest thing he can change. Offered varenicline, patch, quitline. Declines meds, says he'll cut back. Will keep asking.
3. HTN - lower now with metoprolol added.
4. DM2 - A1c in January.
Hospital records re-requested.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Normal axis. ST-segment depression in the lateral leads. No ST elevation. No prior tracing for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Lateral ST depression, consistent with ischemia in the clinical setting.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction 55%. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Valves without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Outside emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - outside hospital
Visit date: 10/08/2025, arrival 14:05
CC: chest discomfort
HPI: 66 y/o M with PAD, HTN, DM2, HLD and a TIA this spring. Several hours of a tight, squeezing pressure behind the breastbone, at times spreading to the left shoulder.
Home meds: amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID with meals, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI at 54, died suddenly at 61; mother stroke at 74, HTN; brother DM2, HTN.
SH: tobacco use.
Data: high-sensitivity troponin I 1,240 ng/L. ECG with ST depressions laterally.
MDM: Non-ST-elevation MI. Aspirin given, clopidogrel load, heparin infusion started, cardiology consulted.
Disposition: admitted to CCU.

documents.title: Outside hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - outside hospital
Admitted 10/08/2025, discharged 10/11/2025.
Diagnosis: NSTEMI.
Course: Admitted to the CCU on dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin plus clopidogrel 600 mg load, then 75 mg daily), atorvastatin 80 mg, beta-blocker, and IV unfractionated heparin by weight-based protocol. aPTT the next morning was in the therapeutic range. Coronary angiography 10/09 via right radial access: 90% stenosis of the mid left circumflex, treated with one drug-eluting stent with an excellent result; no other flow-limiting stenosis. Heparin stopped after the procedure. Echocardiogram LVEF 55%. Telemetry without arrhythmia. Ambulating without symptoms by day 3.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months, do not interrupt without cardiology input; atorvastatin 80 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily; nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN chest pain; amlodipine 10 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiology 4-6 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks; cardiac rehabilitation referral placed. Smoking cessation counseled.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital records 10/8-10/11 reviewed. Mid LCx DES. EF 55%. Discharge meds match what we reconciled 10/21. Clopidogrel planned 12 months (to ~10/2026).

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (annual)
Comparison: 11/13/2024 and 11/08/2023.

documents.title: Cardiac rehabilitation progress report
documents.author: cardiac rehabilitation
documents.body:
CARDIAC REHABILITATION - 30-day progress report
Diagnosis: NSTEMI with PCI to LCx, 10/2025.
Enrolled 11/2025, attending most scheduled sessions (missed a few for snow). Treadmill and bike, gradually increased workload. No angina, arrhythmia or abnormal BP response during exercise. Allergies: NKDA.
Risk factors: continues to smoke; referred to our cessation counselor, declined.
Plan: continue program, reassess at 60 days.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out from the MI. Going to rehab twice a week, likes the staff. Saw cardiology in November - says no changes, keep everything the same; we never got that note. No chest pain, no nitro used. A little less winded on the bike than at the start. No bleeding on the two blood thinners.
Smoking: still about a pack a day. Not willing to use anything to quit.
Meds: aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin 80, metoprolol succ 25, amlodipine 10, metformin 1000 BID, NTG prn.
Exam: vitals flowsheet. Cor RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Feet warm, pulses diminished bilat, no lesions.
A/P
- CAD s/p mid LCx DES 10/2025, old NSTEMI: problem list updated. Continue DAPT through ~10/2026 per cardiology, statin, BB.
- DM2: A1c today.
- Lipids on atorva 80 today.
- Tobacco: counseled.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.body: Mail-order asking us to take over clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25 and atorvastatin 80 (hospital scripts running out). PCP ok'd 90 days + 1 refill each. Pt notified by voicemail.

documents.title: Pt call - hospitalized for leg
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called on his way home from the hospital. Went to the ED Sunday night 4/26 with sudden bad pain and a cold left foot. Told it was a clot in the leg artery; vascular surgery operated that night to take the clot out. Home today. Same pills as before per him, nothing new. Foot feels normal now, incision sore. Requested records. Post-hospital visit set for 5/5 with PCP.

documents.title: Outside emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - outside hospital
Visit date: 04/26/2026, arrival 21:20
CC: left leg pain
HPI: 67-year-old man with PAD, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, a prior TIA and a prior NSTEMI. Six hours ago the left leg became suddenly and severely painful; rest has not helped, and the foot feels cold.
PSH: right femoral-popliteal bypass.
Home meds: amlodipine 10 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice daily with meals; atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime; aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI 54, sudden cardiac arrest death 61; mother ischemic stroke 74, HTN; older brother DM2, HTN.
SH: history of smoking.
Exam: Left foot pale and cool, with weaker pulses than the right. Decreased sensation of the left foot. Dorsiflexion and plantar flexion 3/5 on the left. Capillary refill delayed. ABI 0.5 left, 0.9 right.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, Hct 39.8, WBC 7.2, Plt 210. Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.1, glucose 162.
Bedside arterial Doppler: monophasic signal in the left popliteal artery.
Impression: acute arterial thrombosis/embolism, left lower extremity, with threatened limb.
Plan: heparin bolus and infusion; vascular surgery emergently consulted; to OR.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record 4/26 received; their home med list is outdated (still atorva 40, no clopidogrel/metoprolol). Operative note and discharge summary still outstanding.

events.reason: Post-hospital follow-up, left leg arterial clot

conditions.label: Embolism and thrombosis of arteries of the lower extremities
conditions.note: acute, left leg; thromboembolectomy 4/26/26 at outside hospital

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. RN call 4/30 day of discharge.
We have the ED note only. Per Walter: vascular surgery took him to the OR the same night and pulled the clot out through the groin and behind the knee; when he woke up the foot was warm and pink, and by discharge the numbness and weakness were gone. Heart monitor the whole stay was normal rhythm, and the heart ultrasound showed no clot, he was told. They never found where it came from. Discharged 4/30 on his same meds - nothing added, nothing stopped. Vascular follow-up 6/2.
Today: incisions sore, walking around the apartment and to the car. Foot feels normal. No chest pain.
Exam: vitals flowsheet. L groin and L medial knee incisions clean, staples out, mild bruising, no drainage. L foot warm, pink, cap refill brisk, sensation and strength normal. R leg incisions old and healed.
Meds (bottles): aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, atorvastatin 80, metoprolol succ 25, amlodipine 10, metformin 1000 BID, NTG prn.
A/P
1. Acute arterial thrombosis/embolism L leg s/p thromboembolectomy - added to list. Antiplatelets and statin as per vascular. Vascular 6/2.
2. Smoking - he looked at me and said 'I know.' Discussed again; quitline number given. Declines meds.
3. Re-requested operative note and discharge summary.
4. CBC and BMP today after surgery and on two antiplatelets.

documents.title: Outside vascular surgery follow-up
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - POSTOPERATIVE VISIT
Date of service: 06/02/2026
S/p emergent left femoral-popliteal thromboembolectomy 04/26/2026 for acute limb ischemia. Etiology undetermined; sinus rhythm throughout admission, TTE LVEF 55% without LV thrombus.
Doing well, walking daily, no rest pain.
Meds: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, atorvastatin 80, metoprolol succinate 25, amlodipine 10, metformin. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: left groin and knee incisions healed. Left foot warm, good color, Doppler signals at DP and PT. Left ABI 0.85.
Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel and statin. Walking program. Stop smoking - discussed at length. Arterial duplex surveillance in 6 months.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vascular note 6/2 reviewed. L ABI 0.85 post-op. Duplex in ~6 mo through them. Op note and discharge summary never came - no further request.

documents.title: Walking
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Vascular doc says walk every day. Is it ok if I go back to doing the rail trail, about 2 miles? Heart rehab finished in the winter.

documents.title: RE: Walking
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - the trail is a great idea. Start with what feels comfortable and build up. Stop and call if you get chest pressure, or if the left foot gets cold, numb or painful. Carry your nitro.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Walking the rail trail most mornings, up to two miles, no leg pain, no chest pressure. Hasn't used nitroglycerin. Taking everything. Bruises easily on the two antiplatelets, nothing worse. Still smoking a pack a day.
O: Vitals flowsheet. Cor regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. L groin and knee incisions well healed. Both feet warm, no lesions, monofilament intact, pedal pulses diminished bilaterally, L DP/PT dopplerable per vascular.
A/P
1. Acute L leg arterial thrombosis - treated, recovered. Marked resolved; PAD and vascular follow-up continue (duplex ~Dec).
2. CAD s/p LCx stent - DAPT; cardiology seeing him in August, they will decide clopidogrel duration.
3. DM2 - A1c today. Metformin.
4. HTN - at goal on amlodipine + metoprolol.
5. Lipids on atorva 80 today.
6. Tobacco - counseled; declines pharmacotherapy.
Flu/COVID at the October visit. RTC Oct.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Walter, your labs look good. A1c 7.4, holding steady. LDL cholesterol 64 on the higher atorvastatin, right where we want it after a heart attack. Kidney function and potassium are normal. Keep walking. See you in October.

documents.title: Clopidogrel refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Mail order says no refills left on the clopidogrel. About 10 days of pills. Heart doc appointment is the 11th.

documents.title: RE: Clopidogrel refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent a 90-day supply to the mail-order pharmacy, and I'll have your local pharmacy fill a short supply so you don't run out. Keep taking it until cardiology tells you otherwise.

documents.title: Outside cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY OFFICE VISIT
Date of service: 08/11/2026
CAD s/p DES to mid LCx 10/2025 for NSTEMI; PAD with right fem-pop bypass 2019 and left femoral-popliteal thromboembolectomy 04/2026; TIA (amaurosis fugax) 05/2025.
No angina. Walking 2 miles daily. No bleeding beyond easy bruising.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, NTG SL PRN. NKDA.
Exam: BP and heart rate acceptable. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Assessment: stable after NSTEMI and recent limb ischemia.
Plan: continue current regimen; duration of clopidogrel to be decided at the next visit in light of the April limb event. Continue to urge smoking cessation. Return in 3 months.
